full_judgment:
The petitioner has obtained this Rule against an order dated 19.11.1986 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Cox's Bazar in Criminal Appeal No. 48 of 1986, dismissing the appeal summarily on the ground oflimitation. The appeal was against an order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate, First Class, Upazila Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code sentencing the petitioner to suffer rigorous impnsonment for three years and also to pay a fine of Tk. 3,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more. 

 4. As the petitioner did not appear before the learned Magistrate he believed that the petitioner has absconded or has concealed himself so that he could not be arrested and produced for trial and as there was no immediate prospect of arresting him the learned Magistrate only by Gazette Notification as envisaged in section 339B (1) Cr.P.C. directed the accused petitioner to appear before him by 16.6.85. But there was no publication of the said order in any daily newspaper as contemplated in the said section. By orders dated 5.11.85 and 23.11.85 the Court directed trial of the petitioner in absentia and framed against him charges under sections 420/406 of the Penal Code. And on trial in absentia the learned Magistrate found the petitioner guilty of the charges framed against him and convicted and sentenced him as stated earlier by his order dated 16.1.1986. Against that order of conviction and sentence the petitioner filed Criminal Appeal No. 48 of 1986 in the Court of Sessions Judge. As the appeal was out of time he filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in the filing the appeal. But the learned Sessions Judge rejected the application and dismissed the appeal summarily on the ground of limitation. 

 5. Mr. Abu Bakar Siddiqui, appearing in support of this Rule, submits that the learned Sessions Judge illegally dismissed the appeal summarily holding that the appeal is barred by limitation. The learned Advocate placed before me section 339B Cr.P.C. and submits that provision of said section casts a duty upon the Court to publish the order of the Court directing the accused to appear before the trial Court on a date specified in the order in the official Gazette as well as at least in the Bengali daily newspaper. But in this case the trial Court only published such order in the official Gazette and there being no publication in the daily Bengali newspaper there was failure on the part of the learned Magistrate to comply with the mandatory provision of section 339B. Section 339B Cr.P.C. reads as follows: 

 7. Mr. Karim opposed this Rule and contends that section 339B Cr.P.C. is synonymous with sections 87 and 88 Cr.P.C. He submits that section 87 speaks of proclamation and also speaks for fixing a date of appearance of the accused before the court issuing such proclamations. Having referred to section 87 Mr. Karim relied upon section 537 Cr.P.C. to argue that in view of provision of section 537 Cr.P.C. the order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate shall not be reversed or altered on appeal or on revision on account of omission to publish the order in one Bengali newspaper as required under section 339B Cr.P.C. It. appears that section 537 was on the statute book prior to insertion of section 339B on 30.12.1982 by Ordinance No. XVI of 1982. Therefore, it seems to me that at the time of insertion of section 339B the lawmakers were aware about the existence of section 537 Cr.P.C. but while inserting section 339B in Cr.P.C. they did not consciously make any corresponding amendment in section 537 to include the word 'Gazette Notification and at least one Bengali newspaper'. Considering from this angle I have no hesitation to hold that section 537 does not cover the case falling under section 339B Cr.P.C. Moreover the expression used in section 87 Cr.P.C. is different from the language used in section 339B. In section 87 the word 'may' has been used while in section 339B the word 'shall' has been used. The expression "in at least one Bengali daily newspaper" occurring in section 339B Cr.P.C. seems to me that the provision of section 339B is a mandatory and not a directory one. Thus it b appears in this case that an important question of law has been raised touching the very legality or otherwise of the trial itself before the learned Magistrate. In this view of the matter I hold that in this case the learned Sessions Judge ought to have condoned the delay and should not have dismissed the appeal summarily without deciding the same on merit. I, therefore, set aside the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge on 19.11.1986 dismissing the appeal summarily on the ground of limitation. I condone the delay in filing the Criminal Appeal No. 48 of 1986 and direct the learned Sessions Judge to hear the appeal on merit in accordance with law.
